content: 1. A mechanism should be established to allow service users and providers to submit complaints to management, ensuring accountability and redress in cases of mistreatment or violations. 2. Informed consent procedures must be implemented to ensure that patients are fully aware of and agree to medical interventions. 3. There is no direct evidence on the impact of Respectful Maternity Care (RMC) on equity. However, qualitative reviews suggest that mistreatment and abuse by healthcare workers are significant barriers to the use of facility-based birth services in lowand middle-income countries (LMICs). This contributes to health inequities. 4. Respecting the culture, values, and beliefs of individual women and local communities is highly valued by women. Providing the same standard of maternity care for all, regardless of age, ethnicity, race, sexuality, religion, socioeconomic status, HIV status, language, or other characteristics, is also important. 5. Judgmental care from healthcare providers can lead to inequity. Ensuring non-judgmental care may improve equity, though evidence supporting this is limited. 6. Women across various countries and settings appreciate RMC, and stakeholders emphasize its importance. However, in resource-limited environments, healthcare providers may perceive RMC as increasing their workload, potentially compromising care for other patients. 7. A human rights-based approach to health focuses on empowering women to claim their rights, addressing social determinants of health, and ensuring non-discrimination, transparency, participation, and accountability in health systems. 8. Effective communication between maternity care providers and women in labor is recommended. This includes introducing themselves, addressing women by name, providing clear and concise information, respecting preferences, supporting emotional needs, and ensuring informed consent. 9. Training maternity care staff in interpersonal communication and counseling skills is essential to meet national competency standards. 10. Evidence on the impact of effective communication on birth outcomes is limited. Studies show mixed results regarding women’s satisfaction with communication and care following training interventions. 11. Women value the support and reassurance of healthcare professionals who are sensitive to their needs, especially during labor and childbirth. They also appreciate receiving relevant information in an understandable manner. 12. Effective communication is consistently valued as a key component of RMC. However, no research evidence on the cost or cost-effectiveness of communication interventions was found. 13. Communication interventions are likely to be cost-effective if they improve the quality of maternity care.
